reasons: Datadog system.cpu.iowait is a percent value per host, averaged across CPUs, and the max is taken over hosts. The candidate takes max over every per-CPU series, which yields the busiest single core rather than the host average, so the aggregation differs.
Units differ: Datadog reports percent (0-100) while system.cpu.utilization is a ratio (unit '1'). The x100 scale cannot be applied in promql, so this needs a note and a documented scale.

The series grain differs: the candidate works on per-cpu series, while Datadog works on per-host series. The label that would collapse them is cpu_logical_number, and it needs an avg by host step before the max.
The candidate's cpu_mode="wait" matcher is valid for the observed label cpu_mode. The template variable $scope has no prefix and default '*', so it is correctly dropped.
